title: The last problem
setting: Monday evening at the café where Sora works part-time. Mai drops in on her way home from work and finds Sora on his break, frowning over a sheet of maths homework.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, sora-kun. kyuukei totteru no? sore, nani?
lines.ja: あ、ソラくん。休憩取ってるの？それ、何？
lines.kana: あ、そらくん。きゅうけいとってるの？それ、なに？
lines.english: Oh, Sora. Are you on your break? What's that?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a, mai-san. kore? suugaku no shukudai.
lines.ja: あ、マイさん。これ？数学の宿題。
lines.kana: あ、まいさん。これ？すうがくのしゅくだい。
lines.english: Oh, hi Mai. This? Maths homework.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e? sora-kun ga shukudai shiteru no?
lines.ja: え？ソラくんが宿題してるの？
lines.kana: え？そらくんがしゅくだいしてるの？

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: chigau chigau, kenji-kun no da yo. yuki-san ni tanomarete, kayoubi to kin'youbi ni benkyou oshieteru n da.
lines.ja: 違う違う、ケンジくんのだよ。ユキさんに頼まれて、火曜日と金曜日に勉強教えてるんだ。
lines.kana: ちがうちがう、けんじくんのだよ。ゆきさんにたのまれて、かようびときんようびにべんきょうおしえてるんだ。
lines.english: No, no, it's Kenji's. Yuki asked me to help him study, so I tutor him on Tuesdays and Fridays.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: aa, kenji-kun ne. jibun de shukudai shinai no?
lines.ja: ああ、ケンジくんね。自分で宿題しないの？
lines.kana: ああ、けんじくんね。じぶんでしゅくだいしないの？
lines.english: Oh, Kenji. Doesn't he do his homework on his own?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: shukudai wa chanto suru n da yo. demo, dasu no o wasurechau n da.
lines.ja: 宿題はちゃんとするんだよ。でも、出すのを忘れちゃうんだ。
lines.kana: しゅくだいはちゃんとするんだよ。でも、だすのをわすれちゃうんだ。
lines.english: Oh, he does his homework all right. He just forgets to hand it in.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, shukudai shita noni, dasanai no?
lines.ja: え、宿題したのに、出さないの？
lines.kana: え、しゅくだいしたのに、ださないの？
lines.english: What, he does the homework and then doesn't hand it in?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: sou na n da yo. dakara seiseki ga yokunakute, yuki-san ga shinpai shiteru n da.
lines.ja: そうなんだよ。だから成績がよくなくて、ユキさんが心配してるんだ。
lines.kana: そうなんだよ。だからせいせきがよくなくて、ゆきさんがしんぱいしてるんだ。
lines.english: I know. So his grades aren't good, and Yuki's worried about him.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: jaa, ashita, shukudai chanto dashita ka, kiite mitara?
lines.ja: じゃあ、明日、宿題ちゃんと出したか、聞いてみたら？
lines.kana: じゃあ、あした、しゅくだいちゃんとだしたか、きいてみたら？
lines.english: Then why not ask him tomorrow whether he actually handed it in?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un, sou suru. de, ashita no mondai o saki ni toitoku n da kedo, saigo no ga tokenai n da yo.
lines.ja: うん、そうする。で、明日の問題を先に解いとくんだけど、最後のが解けないんだよ。
lines.kana: うん、そうする。で、あしたのもんだいをさきにといとくんだけど、さいごのがとけないんだよ。
lines.english: Yeah, I will. Anyway, I'm working through tomorrow's problems ahead of time, but I can't get the last one.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: chotto misete. aa, kore, kou yatte toku n ja nai kana. jishin nai kedo.
lines.ja: ちょっと見せて。ああ、これ、こうやって解くんじゃないかな。自信ないけど。
lines.kana: ちょっとみせて。ああ、これ、こうやってとくんじゃないかな。じしんないけど。
lines.english: Let me see. Oh, I think maybe you solve it like this? I'm not sure, though.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e? a, honto da, toketa! mai-san, zettai seiseki yokatta desho?
lines.ja: え？あ、ほんとだ、解けた！マイさん、絶対成績よかったでしょ？
lines.kana: え？あ、ほんとだ、とけた！まいさん、ぜったいせいせきよかったでしょ？
lines.english: Huh? Oh, you're right, I've got it! Mai, I bet you had great grades.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: uun, suugaku dake da yo. hoka wa zenbu dame datta.
lines.ja: ううん、数学だけだよ。ほかは全部ダメだった。
lines.kana: ううん、すうがくだけだよ。ほかはぜんぶだめだった。
lines.english: No, only in maths. I was hopeless at everything else.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: jaa, kondo kenji-kun ni mo oshiete yo. mai-san ga oshietara, kitto seiseki yoku naru yo.
lines.ja: じゃあ、今度ケンジくんにも教えてよ。マイさんが教えたら、きっと成績よくなるよ。
lines.kana: じゃあ、こんどけんじくんにもおしえてよ。まいさんがおしえたら、きっとせいせきよくなるよ。
lines.english: Then come and teach Kenji too sometime. If you taught him, I bet his grades would go up.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, muri muri. watashi, oshieru no nigate da shi.
lines.ja: え、無理無理。私、教えるの苦手だし。
lines.kana: え、むりむり。わたし、おしえるのにがてだし。
lines.english: Oh, no way. I'm no good at teaching.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: jaa, hitotsu dake onegai. boku ga kono mondai tokenakatta koto, kenji-kun ni wa naisho ni shite ne.
lines.ja: じゃあ、一つだけお願い。僕がこの問題解けなかったこと、ケンジくんには内緒にしてね。
lines.kana: じゃあ、ひとつだけおねがい。ぼくがこのもんだいとけなかったこと、けんじくんにはないしょにしてね。
lines.english: Then just one favour. Don't tell Kenji I couldn't solve this one, OK?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, naisho ni shite ageru. demo, koohii ogotte ne.
lines.ja: うん、内緒にしてあげる。でも、コーヒーおごってね。
lines.kana: うん、ないしょにしてあげる。でも、こーひーおごってね。
lines.english: Sure, your secret's safe. But you're buying me a coffee.

choices.english: Mai agrees to come and teach Kenji maths, because her grades were always good.
Sora finds out Kenji never does his homework, so Mai offers to check it for him tomorrow.
Sora is stuck on one of Kenji's maths problems; Mai works it out, and Sora asks her to keep that from Kenji.

questions.explanation: Line 10: Sora is working through Kenji's problems ahead of time but can't get the last one (saigo no ga tokenai). Line 11: Mai shows him how (kou yatte toku), and in line 12 he gets it (toketa). Line 16: he asks her not to tell Kenji he couldn't solve it (naisho ni shite ne), and in line 17 she agrees, for a coffee. A is wrong: Sora does ask her to teach Kenji (line 14), but she says no way, she's bad at teaching (line 15), and her grades were only good in maths (line 13). B is wrong: Kenji does do his homework (line 6, chanto suru); he just forgets to hand it in. And it's Sora who will ask him about it tomorrow (lines 9-10), not Mai.

questions.english: You're taking an evening Japanese class. Sora asks you, "konban hima? issho ni geemu shinai?" Answer that you've got to do your homework, or do it first.
questions.ja: 今晩ひま？一緒にゲームしない？
questions.kana: こんばんひま？いっしょにげーむしない？
questions.romaji: konban hima? issho ni geemu shinai?
questions.answer: Say you've got to do your homework with shukudai and suru: shukudai shinakya (I've got to do my homework), or say yes but do it first: saki ni shukudai shichau (I'll get my homework done first). In casual speech the o drops.

modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今晩は宿題しなきゃ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I've got to do my homework tonight.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, demo saki ni shukudai shichau ne.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、でも先に宿題しちゃうね。
modelAnswers.english: Sure, but let me get my homework done first.

questions.explanation: Doing homework is shukudai o suru, and in casual talk the o drops: Mai asks "sora-kun ga shukudai shiteru no?" in line 3 and "jibun de shukudai shinai no?" in line 5, and Sora says Kenji does do it in line 6 (shukudai wa chanto suru). Don't reach for dasu here: that's handing it in, which is a different step (lines 6-7). Sora is a friend asking casually, so a casual answer fits; yaru also works (shukudai yaranakya).

questions.english: What does Sora say is Kenji's problem with homework?
questions.ja: ソラくんは、ケンジくんの宿題のことを何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらくんは、けんじくんのしゅくだいのことをなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora-kun wa, kenji-kun no shukudai no koto o nan to iimashita ka?

choices.romaji: suru no o wasurechau n da

choices.english: he forgets to hand it in
choices.romaji: dasu no o wasurechau n da

choices.english: he forgets to pass it over (to someone)
choices.romaji: watasu no o wasurechau n da

questions.explanation: Line 6: "shukudai wa chanto suru n da yo. demo, dasu no o wasurechau n da." Handing in homework is dasu (put it out). Mai picks it up in line 7 (shukudai shita noni, dasanai no?) and line 9 (shukudai chanto dashita ka). A is the partner phrase, and Sora says the opposite: Kenji does do it (chanto suru). Doing it and handing it in are two steps, and Kenji only manages the first. C, watasu, is handing something over to a person; turning in schoolwork is dasu.

questions.english: Sora says, "saigo no ga tokenai n da yo." What's he stuck on?
questions.ja: ソラくんは、何に困っていましたか？
questions.kana: そらくんは、なににこまっていましたか？
questions.romaji: sora-kun wa, nani ni komatte imashita ka?

choices.english: He can't work out the last maths problem.
He can't answer the last question Kenji asked him.
He can't get the last of the homework finished before his break ends.

questions.explanation: Line 10: tokenai is the can't-form of toku, and a maths or test problem is something you toku (untie): mondai o toku. He's working out tomorrow's problems ahead of time (saki ni toitoku). Mai shows him how in line 11 (kou yatte toku), he gets it in line 12 (toketa), and in line 16 he asks her not to tell Kenji he couldn't (tokenakatta). B mixes it up with shitsumon ni kotaeru (answer a question someone asks); Kenji isn't there and hasn't asked anything. C: his break comes up in line 1, but nobody mentions it ending, and toku is about solving, not finishing.

questions.english: After Mai answers, Sora turns to you: "sotchi wa? seiseki yokatta?" Tell him about your own grades at school, and play it down the way Mai does.
questions.ja: そっちは？成績よかった？
questions.kana: そっちは？せいせきよかった？
questions.answer: Use seiseki with ii in the past: yokatta (were good) or yokunakatta (weren't good). It's about you, so keep it modest: say they weren't that good, or name just one subject.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, seiseki wa sonna ni yokunakatta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、成績はそんなによくなかったよ。
modelAnswers.english: Nah, my grades weren't all that good.

modelAnswers.romaji: eigo dake wa seiseki yokatta kedo, hoka wa dame datta.
modelAnswers.ja: 英語だけは成績よかったけど、ほかはダメだった。
modelAnswers.english: My grades were good in English, but the rest were hopeless.

questions.explanation: The grades are the subject and ii describes them: seiseki ga yokunakute (line 8), seiseki yokatta (line 12), seiseki yoku naru (line 14). ii takes its forms from yoi, so it's yokatta and yokunakatta, never iikatta. Don't calque 'get good grades' as ii seiseki o morau. Saying your own grades were good sounds like bragging, which is why Mai plays it down in line 13 (suugaku dake da yo).
